narrative: OMX30 faces significant headwind from synchronized global equity rout—DAX, US indices, and Nikkei all down 2%+ overnight, with ADX showing moderate momentum but bearish directional bias. Technical picture deteriorates sharply: RSI at 35.22 triggers mean-reversion watch, MACD crossed below signal, and price now trades below lower Bollinger Band at -0.07%B, indicating capitulation selling. Stochastic (K=7.2, D=11.4) is deeply oversold, suggesting potential bounce, but weighted correlation bias remains firmly negative at -1.966%. Falling US yields (10Y at 4.992%, -119bp) and collapsing commodities (Gold -2.83%, Oil -3.27%, Copper -1.20%) point to growth concerns overriding yield support. High-beta exporters and cyclicals face immediate pressure; defensive rotation into pharma/healthcare warranted but limited by broad risk-off.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens to brutal global cross-currents: Asia and US equity collapse overnight, DAX -2.04%, NASDAQ -2.25%, Nikkei -5.06% set aggressive tone. Expected OMX30 open in -1.0 to -1.5% range, testing 3085 support (lower Bollinger Band). Technical wash-out evident—RSI 35.22, Stochastic in deep oversold (K=7.2), MACD below signal—points to potential bounce setup mid-session IF intraday stabilizes, but ADX 19.4 with bearish DI bias and VIX 29.76 spike mean conviction low. Watch commodities: Oil -3.27% and Gold -2.83% signal risk-off; USD/SEK strength (+0.38%) offers mild tailwind to exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson) but insufficient to offset sector rotation. Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) face yield headwind from falling 10Y. Key level 3123 (yesterday close) must hold for any floor; break risks 3050. Focus: oversold bounce opportunity into 14:30 US Jobless Claims; avoid new longs until technical wash confirms.
